Title: She wanted to stay home, but a Kuching father’s insistence saved her when their house fell into the river
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 4 — Isniah Daud was tending to her kuih stall with her three daughters when a neighbour called to tell her that their riverside house near Kampung Bintawa Tengah had collapsed into the river yesterday morning.
The 42-year-old immediately left the stall, leaving her daughters to continue tending to it, and rushed home.
Her youngest daughter, 11, had initially wanted to remain at home that morning but eventually followed her mother after her father, Mohd Ismail Mostapha, insisted she go along.
“Good thing my youngest daughter was not at home. At first she wanted to stay in, but my husband insisted she should come with me, so she did,” Isniah told The Borneo Post when met.
Her husband was away doing contract work involving the opening of containers when the incident occurred.
Isniah said she had experienced an unexplained sense of unease shortly before the collapse.
“When I was tending to my kuih stall, I seemed to have a bad feeling but I can’t really explain it.
“Then, all of a sudden, the flour and some coconut water spilled. A friend of mine who also sells kuih there jokingly asked, ‘Why did you play with your flour and your coconut water?’
“About 10 minutes later, a neighbour called me about the incident. I left immediately, leaving my daughters to tend to the stall,” she said.
The family later managed to recover some certificates and important documents from the rubble, but her daughters’ identification cards could not be retrieved as they were inside a bedroom that had been submerged.
“When we checked the rubble, we saw my youngest daughter’s bed impaled by a collapsed pole of the house.
“I was thinking, what if my youngest daughter had stayed in the house today,” she said.
Isniah said the house was about 18 years old, although she had lived there for 14 years after her sister handed it over to her when she built a new house.
She said the family had been concerned about the condition of the riverside house, particularly during rainy weather.
“Since the house is at the riverside, of course it concerns me, especially when there’s rain — we can feel the house shaking.
“We did plan to renovate the house but well, didn’t manage,” she said.
The collapse also damaged a neighbouring house after debris from Isniah’s house struck two of its poles, leaving the structure unstable.
Isniah said firefighters had advised the occupants not to remain in the house.
“As for my family, for now we’re staying at my uncle’s house,” she said.
Isniah, her husband and their three daughters escaped unhurt in the incident.
Her husband later went to the police station to lodge a report, following advice from firefighters and police who attended the scene.
The incident occurred at about 9.30am, with the Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department receiving a report at around 1.16pm before personnel from the Petra Jaya Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene.
The department said no rescue operation was conducted as the five residents – a couple and their three daughters – had managed to escape the collapsed house.
Firefighters also found that a nearby house was at risk of collapse after some of its stilts were struck by debris from the affected house, rendering the structure unstable. Its owner was subsequently advised to exercise caution. — The Borneo Post

Title: Rescued once, stranded again: False killer whale dies at Sarawak beach
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 4 — A false killer whale died yesterday after becoming stranded twice along the Pueh coastline in Sematan.
Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC) general manager Abang Arabi Abang Aimran said the adult female marine mammal was initially rescued and released back into the sea with assistance from the Lundu/Sematan District Civil Defence Force, Royal Malaysia Police and members of the public.
“However, at about 9am, SFC received information from local fishermen that the marine mammal had stranded again near the Pueh Youth Camp Beach area.
“The animal was found in a weak condition and eventually died at about 2pm,” he said in a statement.
Abang Arabi, who is also SFC Sarawak Wildlife controller, said based on its external morphology and number of teeth, the marine mammal was identified as a false killer whale (
Pseudorca crassidens)
, measuring 3.85 metres in length with a body girth of 1.77 metres.
He said SFC subsequently carried out standard operating procedures for stranded marine animals and conducted a necropsy on the carcass.
The examination found shark bite marks on the animal, while its stomach contained very little material mixed with sand.
“This indicates that the animal may not have been able to obtain sufficient food before becoming stranded,” he said.
Based on the necropsy findings, Abang Arabi said the animal’s death was believed to be linked to complications arising from the stranding, including possible circulatory failure caused by heat stress or heat stroke.
Nine SFC personnel, assisted by six residents of Kampung Pueh, were involved in the operation.
Biometric specimens were also collected for SFC’s DNA database for future reference.
Abang Arabi said all marine mammal species, including dolphins, whales and dugongs, are classified as Totally Protected Animals under the Wildlife Protection Ordinance 1998.
He urged members of the public not to handle stranded, injured or dead wildlife themselves, but to immediately report such cases to SFC through its hotline or the nearest SFC Kuching Regional Office.
“This will enable appropriate rescue, examination and management measures to be carried out,” he said.
Abang Arabi added that a false killer whale had previously been recorded as stranded on a beach in Miri in 2013.
He also expressed appreciation to the agencies, local community and members of the public who assisted during the incident. — The Borneo Post

Title: Did you feel that? MetMalaysia says 5.8 Sumatra quake could rattle western peninsular Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — A moderate earthquake measuring 5.8 on the Richter scale was detected in North Sumatra, Indonesia, at 7.37am today.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in a statement today, said the earthquake was centred at coordinates 4.6 degrees north and 96.3 degrees east, at a depth of 30 kilometres (km), about 59km northeast of Meulaboh, Indonesia.
“The tremors may be felt in the western states of peninsular Malaysia,” it said.
However, there is no tsunami threat to Malaysia. — Bernama

Title: In latest lawsuit, family of Bandar Utama school murder victim alleges duty of care breaches by Putrajaya, 17 others
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — The family of 16-year-old Yap Shing Xuen, who was fatally stabbed at a Bandar Utama secondary school last year, has claimed in a lawsuit that breaches of duty of care by the assailant’s parents, school authorities and government agencies contributed to her death.
In the lawsuit filed in the High Court on October 1, Wong Lee Ping and Yap’s sister, Shing Tong, were named as the plaintiffs, with 18 respondents named in the suit.
Among those named are the boy’s parents, the boy himself, and several school authorities, including his homeroom teacher, the school principal, and teachers responsible for counselling and student affairs.
The family also named officers from the Petaling Utama district education office, the Selangor education department director, the director-general of education, the education minister, the registrar general of educational institutions and teachers, the director-general of health, the health minister, the women, family and community Development minister and the government of Malaysia.
Wong, who is also suing as the estate administrator and in her own right, is seeking special damages totalling RM120,602 for Shing Xuen’s funeral expenses from the named defendants jointly and separately.
She is also separately seeking general damages to be assessed by the High Court, including any other relief the court deems fit or appropriate.
In court documents sighted by
Malay Mail
, Wong said the killing could have been prevented if the boy’s family and the government agencies named in the suit had taken preventive measures.
“The first defendant (the boy) had been displaying mental health illness since at least 2020.
“It was reasonably foreseeable by the second and third defendants (the boy’s parents) that the boy had mental health issues and that he could pose a threat to himself and others.
“The same would apply to the fourth and ninth defendants (the school authorities) when the boy had enrolled in the school in or around 2024,” she said.
In her claim against the boy and his parents, Wong said the parents failed to exercise due care as parents and guardians, resulting in the killing, and breached their duty of care by failing to ensure that the boy received proper medical attention.
She also said it was reasonably foreseeable that the named government agencies’ failure to properly implement relevant policies could result in students with mental health conditions posing a safety risk to other students, including physical harm.
Wong said the family’s claim against the school authorities and government agencies was for negligence.
She said intervention measures could have been taken if the necessary steps had been implemented for early detection.
This would have included a more detailed assessment of the boy’s mental health condition, including a psychiatric assessment, which could have led to his removal from the school until that risk to other students’ safety was adequately addressed.
In detailing her losses, Wong said the sudden and senseless loss of Shing Xuen’s life caused her immense grief, as she had raised her as a single mother.
Since the killing, Wong said she had been unable to focus on her work, reducing her income and significantly affecting her livelihood as the family’s primary breadwinner.
As for Shing Xuen’s sister, Wong said she is currently pursuing tertiary education but has been unable to focus on her studies effectively, which affects her academic performance.
Both also said they had yet to fully come to terms with the shock and trauma caused by the killing, adding that they were not mentally prepared to speak to a healthcare professional about their pain and suffering as of the lawsuit filing date.
Lawyer Surendra Ananth, who is representing the family, said the lawsuit is currently scheduled for case management on October 29.

Title: Loke finds upside in DAP setbacks as party navigates new political realities
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 4 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke has described the party’s recent electoral setbacks, including its defeat in Negeri Sembilan, as a “blessing in disguise”, saying the losses have exposed challenges faced by rival political blocs and could ultimately strengthen the party’s position.
Speaking in an interview with
The Straits Times
, the transport minister said DAP remained optimistic despite a series of disappointing election results and growing dissatisfaction among parts of its traditional support base.
Loke pointed to developments in Negeri Sembilan, where he argued that the new state administration had yet to resolve issues it had pledged to address after coming to power. He said the situation demonstrated that political victories did not automatically translate into effective governance.
His remarks come at a critical juncture for DAP, which has transitioned from being a long-time opposition party to a key component of Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s federal administration. The party has faced pressure to balance its reform agenda with the realities of governing within a multi-party coalition.
Loke also addressed criticism surrounding his decision to resign from the Cabinet following the decision to allow former prime minister Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. While some have questioned the timing of his resignation, Loke maintained that he would leave his ministerial post once Najib fulfils the conditions attached to the arrangement, including the settlement of an outstanding RM50 million fine.
He rejected claims that the move was merely political theatre, saying the timeline had been agreed upon with Anwar when he offered his resignation.
Despite recent challenges, Loke expressed confidence that DAP could rebuild support and remain influential within the ruling coalition, arguing that cooperation and compromise would be necessary as Malaysia moves towards its next general election.

Title: Johor police confirm investigating Yong Peng student’s death, public asked to refrain from spreading unverifiable information
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Oct 4 — Johor police have urged the public to give investigators space to conduct a thorough probe into the death of a female student at a secondary school in Yong Peng.
Johor Deputy Police Chief Datuk M. Kumar said authorities are currently investigating the incident and called on the public to refrain from making speculations that could interfere with the investigation process.
He said police are gathering information and examining all aspects of the case to determine the circumstances surrounding the student’s death.
“The investigation is still ongoing. We ask all parties to allow police to carry out their duties and avoid spreading unverified information that could affect the investigation,” he said.
The incident has attracted widespread public attention, but police have yet to disclose further details pending the outcome of investigations.
Kumar said any confirmed developments would be announced once investigations have been completed and relevant facts verified.
Police have assured that the case will be investigated comprehensively and in accordance with existing legal procedures.

Title: Hammer attack leaves Marang man dead, sister injured while trying to intervene
Article:
MARANG, Oct 4 — A man died after he was believed to have been bludgeoned with a hammer by his mentally ill younger brother in an incident at Kampung Tasek, near here yesterday.
The victim, Mohd Nasir Ismail, 43, the eldest of nine siblings, succumbed to severe head injuries in the attack.
The victim’s mother, Hasnah Sulong, 63, who was still in shock over the tragedy, said she was in the living room when she heard screams and the sounds of a struggle from another part of the house.
“I immediately called my husband, Ismail Ibrahim, 80, who was outside the house.
“When he came inside, he saw Nasir covered in blood with severe head injuries,” she said when met at her residence in Kampung Tasek yesterday.
Hasnah said her second child, Affendi, 42, who has a history of mental health issues, is suspected to be involved in the incident.
She added that another child, Rurazmiza, 36, sustained back injuries after being struck with the hammer while trying to stop the fight.
“Rurazmiza tried to step in to break up the fight, but she was also injured when struck,” she said.
Hasnah, a stroke survivor, said the tragedy brought back painful memories of an incident 12 years ago when her husband was stabbed by the same son.
However, that incident did not prevent the family from continuing to care for and live with him.
Marang District Police Chief Supt Saari Mohamed confirmed the incident when contacted. — Bernama

Title: Anwar welcomes Bahrain investment as F1 brings Gulf ties into focus
Article:

Title: WhatsApp location helps rescuers find two lost hikers in Penang Youth Park
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 4 — Two men who lost their way while hiking in Youth Park near the Botanical Gardens here last evening have been found safe.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call regarding the incident at 6.11pm, after which eight personnel and a fire engine from the Bagan Jermal Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene.
“Firefighters conducted a search and rescue (SAR) operation based on the location shared by the victims via WhatsApp, assisted by three police officers.
“Muhammad Hakim Razali and Muhammad Faiz Abdul Wahab, both 25, were found safe at 7.42pm, about two kilometres from the foot of the hill,” he said in a statement last night.
He added that the victims were safely brought down and handed over to the police for further action before the operation ended at 7.50pm. — Bernama

Title: After shuttle chaos, Sepang circuit chief pitches in as F1 fans wait for buses after second race day
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 4 — Sepang International Circuit (SIC) chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif stepped in to help fans who had endured a long wait for shuttle buses following the second day of the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) in Malaysia 2026 yesterday.
Azhan Shafriman and his team were seen on the ground managing the crowd and distributing mineral water to fans waiting for buses, according to posts shared on social media.
One Threads user, @fatinsurayaa_, said Azhan Shafriman and his crew were helping control the crowd and handing out mineral water after some visitors had reportedly fainted.
Another user, @nrfaofdiaries, praised Azhan for personally stepping in to assist fans.
“Honestly, seeing this makes me emotional. Despite everything that happened, SIC’s CEO himself stepped in to manage the crowd and distribute mineral water to fans who needed help,” the post wrote.
Meanwhile, @cxingt described Azhan’s actions as an example of leadership.
Earlier, a social media post showed Azhan Shafriman on the ground to oversee and assist with the flow of buses to the iconic Malaysian circuit.
Several fans praised the improved crowd and traffic management at SIC earlier today, highlighting smoother queues, dedicated lanes for shuttle buses and a stronger presence of staff, marshals and police.
The positive reactions came a day after social media users had highlighted congestion upon leaving SIC, with some reporting lengthy waits for shuttle buses to parking areas and nearby transport hubs.
In July, Formula 1 confirmed Malaysia as the host of the Gulf Air Bahrain GP from Oct 2 to 4, following an agreement between Formula 1, the International Automobile Federation (FIA) and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
The agreement kept the Bahrain GP on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race was cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
Malaysia hosted the Malaysian GP at SIC from 1999 to 2017 before the race was dropped from the F1 calendar. — Bernama

Title: Husband and wife die, five others hurt in head-on crash with 4WD near Sibu roundabout
Article:
SIBU, Oct 4 — A husband and wife were killed after the car they were travelling in collided with a four-wheel-drive (4WD) pickup truck near the Pulau Dudong Roundabout along Jalan Dudong here yesterday afternoon.
The collision left the car badly damaged, while the pickup truck overturned and came to rest on its side against the car.
Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) Zone 4 Sibu chief Andy Alie said the incident was reported at about 4.15pm, with firefighters from Sibu Jaya Fire and Rescue Station arriving at the scene at 4.22pm.
He said the two victims in the car were found trapped and unconscious inside the vehicle.
“Firefighters used rescue tools and a stretcher to extricate both victims from the vehicle.
“Paramedics from Sibu Hospital later confirmed that both victims had succumbed to their injuries,” he said.
The driver was identified as Julaihi Raduan, 52, and his wife, Marliza Salleh, 49.
Andy said the five occupants of the pickup truck – two adults and three children – sustained minor injuries and received initial treatment from paramedics at the scene.
He said the two vehicles were believed to have collided head-on, although the exact circumstances of the crash remained under investigation.
The bodies of the two victims were later handed over to police for further action.
Six firefighters and one Fire Rescue Tender from Sibu Jaya Bomba Station were involved in the operation.
Meanwhile, Sibu police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad, when contacted, confirmed the incident.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. — The Borneo Post

Title: Police probe involving Caprice over alleged document disclosure now under DPP review
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — An investigation paper (IP) into a police report lodged by businessman Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan over the alleged disclosure of an official document is now under review by the Selangor Deputy Public Prosecutor’s Office.
Jeyenderan’s lawyer, Muniandy Vestanathan, said his firm had received a letter dated Aug 28, 2026, signed by Selangor Criminal Investigation Department chief SAC Zulkarnain Samsudin, on the status of the investigation.
“The letter stated that the IP was sent to the Selangor Deputy Public Prosecutor’s Office on July 28, 2026, for advice and further instructions, and is currently under legal review by the office,” he told Malay Mail.
Muniandy said the letter indicated that the investigation was being conducted under Section 203A of the Penal Code, which concerns disclosure of information, and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
Jeyenderan, the chief executive officer of Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, lodged the report at the Ampang Jaya District Police Headquarters on Sept 3 last year over the alleged disclosure of an official document by social media personality Caprice, whose real name is Ariz Ramli.
“My client made the report on Sept 3 last year and it has been a year since we have been waiting for a response. We are therefore seeking an update on the current status of the case and whether any further instructions have been issued by the DPP’s Office,” Muniandy said.
The police investigation is separate from civil proceedings involving Jeyenderan and Ariz, which Muniandy said are scheduled to begin in February 2027 at the Kuala Lumpur High Court.
The allegations have not been established in court, and no finding of criminal wrongdoing has been made against Ariz in relation to the investigation, which remains subject to the relevant legal and prosecutorial processes.

Title: Senior Citizens Bill to strengthen protection for older Malaysians, says Nancy Shukri
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 3 — The physical and mental well-being of senior citizens will be among the key areas addressed under the Senior Citizens Bill, which is expected to be tabled in the Cabinet soon, said Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri.
She said the bill was being drafted to ensure senior citizens receive adequate protection in various aspects of life, enabling them to enjoy a better quality of life.
“The government already has policies and frameworks in place for senior citizens, and this bill is a follow-up measure to further strengthen their protection.
“The bill specifically focuses on safeguarding senior citizens so that they are protected in all aspects,” she told reporters after officiating the 2026 National-Level Senior Citizens Day celebration at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) in Ayer Keroh here today.
Also present was Social Welfare Department (JKM) director-general Datuk Che Murad Sayang RamJanuary
Nancy said the bill reflected the government’s commitment to strengthening support, protection and care systems for senior citizens, ensuring they remain relevant to current needs and future demographic changes in the country.
She added that senior citizens should not be regarded as a burden, but instead valued and encouraged to serve as role models for the younger generation, in line with efforts to strengthen family values.
Commenting on the issue of independent speakers, Nancy said her ministry was ready to cooperate with relevant parties to screen individuals appointed to deliver talks to ensure they had the necessary qualifications and calibre.
“It would not be entirely appropriate for us to take over the responsibility (of conducting the screenings) as the matter comes under the purview of other agencies or ministries. However, we can work together by reminding those organising such talks to ensure that the speakers are of high calibre,” she said.
According to media reports, police received a report on September 26 over an allegation of sexual harassment of a child by a motivational speaker.
Perlis police chief DCP Hamzah Hashim said the report was lodged at 2.09am and the case was being investigated under Section 12 of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017. — Bernama

Title: Anwar visits Sepang for F1 GP qualifying round, attends welcome dinner hosted by Bahrain crown prince
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 3 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today attended the Formula One (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix qualifying session at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), where he also inspected preparations and the overall running of the race.
Anwar arrived at the circuit at about 4.50pm and was received by Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Petronas President and Group Chief Executive Officer Tan Sri Tengku Muhammad Taufik, SIC Chairman Datin Anita Azrina Abdul Aziz and other dignitaries.
He then proceeded for a 15-minute tour of the Mercedes-AMG Petronas team pit.
Following the session, Anwar attended a welcome dinner hosted by Crown Prince and Prime Minister of Bahrain Prince Salman bin Hamad Al-Khalifa at the paddock.
The F1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia began yesterday with the first and second free practice sessions, followed by the third free practice session and qualifying today.
The 56-lap race is scheduled to start at 3pm tomorrow.
The event marks the return of Formula One to Sepang after a nine-year absence, with the circuit last hosting an F1 race in 2017.
In July, Formula 1 and the International Automobile Federation (FIA) confirmed that Malaysia would host the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2 to 4, following an agreement involving F1, the FIA and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
The arrangement enables the Bahrain Grand Prix to remain on the 2026 F1 calendar after the original event could not proceed in Bahrain, with the race relocated to Sepang amid the situation in West Asia.
The return of Formula One to Malaysia followed discussions and cooperation involving His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and King Hamad bin Isa Al-Khalifa of Bahrain, as well as the two governments.
Formula One made its debut at Sepang in 1999, with the circuit hosting the Malaysian Grand Prix until 2017. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia aims for economic resilience over efficiency amid global uncertainties, says Tengku Zafrul
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Malaysia’s economic focus has shifted from pursuing efficiency to building greater resilience as the country continues to outperform growth forecasts despite global uncertainty, the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) said.
Mida chairman Datuk Seri Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz said economic leadership also meant preparing Malaysia to seize clear opportunities while remaining resilient to unpredictable shocks.
He said key fiscal reforms, including fuel subsidy rationalisation and the Fiscal Responsibility Act, had strengthened Malaysia’s public finances.
“But economic reform must be matched by compassion; we must safeguard the vulnerable while building national capacity.
“We must proactively lift incomes by ensuring wages rise alongside productivity, creating higher-paying jobs and boosting entrepreneurship,” he said in his special leadership address at the Youth Economic Forum here today.
The former Investment, Trade and Industry Minister said trade routes were being redrawn while artificial intelligence (AI) was both empowering and disrupting the workforce, reshaping jobs that had once provided young people with their first foothold in a career.
Tengku Zafrul said Malaysia’s young population could become an economic dividend only if it translated into higher productivity, innovation, high-value jobs and new businesses.
“As record investment flows into our region and our country, we must keep asking: what does this investment create for Malaysians? How many high-income jobs? How many young engineers with new skills? How many small and medium-sized enterprises plugged into global supply chains?
“Capital should build stronger firms, and technology should build better skills,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Anwar calls on young Malaysians to master AI and new tech to drive economic growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged Malaysia’s youth to master emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) and quantum computing to drive economic growth.
He said young people must be prepared to explore new fields of knowledge to ensure the country’s technological advancement is guided by its own values, ethics and principles.
“Digital transformation requires AI. Otherwise, we will fall behind in development and in our ability to strengthen the economy.
“I said recently in Shanghai, when I was with Chinese Premier (Li Qiang), that we must master AI. Otherwise, AI will master us,” he said.
Anwar was speaking at the opening of the Youth Economic Forum 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre today.
Also present were Youth and Sports Minister Mohammed Taufiq Johari, political secretary to the finance minister Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim, Perdana Fellows Alumni Association president Fanitsyara Kam Phon, and Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz.
Anwar said while digital transformation and high-technology economic development were essential, such progress should not come at the expense of ethics, morality and human values.
“Reach for the skies, but remain rooted in the ground. That means new technology, new sciences, new research ... but do not let AI erode moral, ethical and human values,” he said.
Anwar said the government would continue to improve the quality of education, strengthen proficiency in Bahasa Melayu and English, and give young Malaysians opportunities to master other languages, including Chinese, Tamil, Arabic, French and German.
He also urged young people to exercise critical thinking and not become “tools” or blindly devoted to any particular individual or political party.
Instead, he urged the younger generation to be devoted to truth, justice, the pursuit of knowledge and integrity as they work to lead the country towards greater success.
“I am confident that if this is the new spirit, we will see our country move forward at speed and, within 10 years, we will no longer recognise the Malaysia of today. Instead, we will see a new, vibrant, progressive and successful Malaysia,” he said. — Bernama

Title: PAS leaders missed Dr Hasmah’s funeral due to prior commitments, says Tuan Ibrahim
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said most PAS leaders could not attend Tun Dr Hasmah Mohd Ali’s funeral because they had prior commitments at home and abroad.
The party’s deputy president said PAS had conveyed its condolences directly to former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his family, according to
Sinar Harian
.
“We acknowledge that most PAS leaders had specific programmes on the day she passed away,” he said at a press conference for the Zulkifli Muhammad Islamic Studies Convocation Ceremony (KUIZM) in Gombak today.
Tuan Ibrahim, who is also Perikatan Nasional’s Pahang chairman, said the absence was not deliberate.
He cited his own involvement in a programme in Kelantan, along with Secretary-General Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan and Vice-President Datuk Mohd Amar Abdullah.
“Thus, their absence was indeed due to unavoidable programmes,” he said.
PAS sent Muslimat wing chief and Central Committee member Datuk Seri Shahidan Kassim, and joined the tahlil at Dr Mahathir’s home, he said.
Tuan Ibrahim said Dr Hasmah’s death is unexpected and her burial must be expedited without waiting for anyone.
“Sometimes a father dies but the child cannot make it in time because the death was sudden,” he said.
“We cannot wait long because when someone dies, the body must be buried quickly.”
He said the party had conveyed its condolences on behalf of PAS.
“May he (Dr Mahathir) be patient with what has happened, and what matters is that we pray that the soul of the late Dr Hasmah be blessed and placed among the righteous servants of Allah,” he said.
Dr Hasmah died at the National Heart Institute (IJN) at 9.20am on September 28, as reported by Sinar Harian.
Her son, Tan Sri Mokhzani Mahathir, confirmed the news of the passing of the 100-year-old.
Dr Hasmah was born on July 12, 1926, and married Tun Dr Mahathir on August 5, 1956.

Title: ‘Will my job still exist in 10 years’ time?’: Ahead of Budget 2027, youth minister sums up young Malaysians’ fears
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Malaysian youths today have three main concerns, including whether their existing jobs would still exist in the next decade, Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said today.
Speaking at the Perdana Fellows Alumni Association’s (PFAA) Youth Economic Forum 2026 (YEF 2026), Dr Taufiq said his ministry had been part of a Budget roadshow in six zones nationwide to engage with youths ahead of the government’s upcoming Budget 2027.
He noted that the youths did not ask theoretical questions, and summarised their questions as revolving around three main concerns.
“Firstly, can youths bear the cost of living?
“Secondly, will my job today still exist 10 years from now? And the third question that is frequently mentioned by youths, if I fall, who will help me?” he said ahead of the tabling of the government’s Budget 2027 in Parliament next Friday.
Dr Taufiq said the panel discussions at today’s YEF on artificial intelligence, talent, green energy and social protection would answer these questions, as youths would not feel the benefits of government policies if those policies fail to address their anxieties.
While saying that youths are often told to be strong and to upskill themselves, Dr Taufiq said that being strong or resilient is not a policy.
“Being strong is what the public is forced to do temporarily while they wait for policies to come. Our duty is to create a protection system that is strong enough so that Malaysia’s youths do not have to ‘bersusah payah’ (toil) to be heroes just to continue living,” he said.
He added that the federal government is currently working on raising both the ceiling and the floor of the economy to ensure that all citizens feel the benefits from foreign direct investments into Malaysia.
He thanked the youths for their proposals on developing the country, and expressed hope that they could also help build the nation together.
At the YEF 2026, which carried the theme of “Decoding the Next Decade: Advancing Malaysia’s Economic Frontier”, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim received six policy proposals that the PFAA had developed based on a nationwide survey of more than 2,000 youths.
The six proposals covered artificial intelligence (AI), green entrepreneurship, skills development, better public services, foreign direct investment, and establishing a National Youth Economic Action Council to give youths a permanent platform to make economic policies.
Anwar also received a memorandum on the youths’ proposals for Budget 2027 at the forum.

Title: Anwar’s nutmeg story: PM says grandmother’s childhood lesson on theft behind his anti-graft stance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said he, as the prime minister, would not allow anyone to embezzle or steal money, recalling a lesson from his own childhood as he continued his firm stance against corruption in Malaysia.
Anwar today described a lesson he had learnt from his grandmother when he was a primary school student aged around eight or nine, after he took nutmegs from a small farm on a hill in Bukit Mertajam, Penang.
Anwar described his grandmother’s questioning, where he confirmed he did not buy and also did not get permission to take those nutmegs from a farm.
“But I said ‘Chinese farm’. So I thought Chinese farm, Malay steal, it’s ok. I was aged eight or nine,” he said in his speech at the Youth Economic Forum (YEF) 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre.
“My grandmother said ‘No, if they are taken without permission, from whoever it is, even if they were four nutmegs, it is theft. And stealing is a sin,” he said.
Anwar said he had then decided to not eat the nutmegs and to return them the next day, but said his grandmother had insisted that he return them the same day itself.
Recalling that it was nearly 7pm and with all his friends having already returned home, Anwar said he then ran uphill in the dark and that he had felt afraid when he heard the sound of dogs.
“I took the four nutmegs and threw them back to that area. I ran back and cried, because I did not understand why my grandmother was so firm in ensuring discipline, because I stole four nutmegs and I can return them tomorrow.
“But that taught me, when (I) become prime minister, don’t steal and don’t allow others to steal,” he said to loud claps from the youth gathered at the plenary hall in KLCC.
He said he hoped youths would understand why it is important to master knowledge and also know what is considered wrong, and also urged them to maintain their values.
Before sharing his childhood story, Anwar had alluded to those who are corrupt when saying that Malaysia is not poor, but that the country had lost billions of its riches due to the practices of “
penyakau
” (thieves).
He urged youths in Malaysia to rise up to reject corruption, urging them not to compromise against “penyakau”.
Countering those who might accuse him of highlighting politics to youths, Anwar said youths may not be vocal, but are aware that theft is wrong.
He pointed out that even stealing a pencil or pen in school would result in reprimand from teachers, and questioned how stealing billions of ringgit when one has grown up to be a leader would be morally or ethically acceptable.
Earlier in his speech, Anwar emphasised the importance of morals and criticised those who may consider corruption acceptable as it involves their own race.
“There are people who told me, ‘This Datuk Anwar highlights corruption issues — 1MDB, Tabung Haji, Felda. These are Malay bodies. Don’t criticise, these are Malay bodies’. So if it’s Malay bodies, can ‘
songlap
’, ‘
sakau
’? Where did you learn this from? This is a damaged way of thinking,” he said.
The words “
songlap
” and “
sakau
” are generally used to refer to theft, with Anwar saying that Malaysia has the capability to rise further but that billions had been lost through 1Malaysia Development Berhad, Lembaga Tabung Haji and Felda.
Anwar said he was highlighting all these to the youth as he believes they still have idealism and want the country to be dignified, also believing that they “hate misappropriation, corruption and leaders who use their powers to gain riches”.
“Because the youths know many are still good, will uplift those who are good and reject those who are clearly corrupt and abused their powers,” Anwar said to loud cheers and claps from the youths gathered here.

Title: Seeing parents pinned in the car on video call is what broke us, daughter says after Johor crash
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Oct 3 — The daughter of a couple who died in a road crash at Kilometre 72.5 of Jalan Batu Pahat-Mersing yesterday never expected an incident she initially thought was minor to claim her parents’ lives.
Ain Zanariah Mislan, 33, said she received news that her mother, Nor Azilah A Rahman, 49, and father, Mislan Osman, 54, had been killed after their car collided with a lorry while they were returning home from Endau, Mersing, after sending off her grandmother.
She was at work when she received the call at about 5.30pm. Her husband, Mohd Hazerul, 33, then broke the news that her parents had died, while her two younger sisters, who were also in the Hyundai Matrix, were injured.
“At first, I thought it was just a minor accident... my husband tried calling my sister’s mobile phone, but someone else answered and said our parents had been pronounced dead at the scene. The person who answered was a driver right behind their car.
“We also made a video call with the woman we called ‘akak’. What broke our hearts most was seeing our parents pinned inside the car ourselves,” she said at her residence in Kampung Parit Pulai, near here today.
According to Ain Zanariah, her husband said her father had flashed an unusually different smile the morning before the accident, before they left for Mersing at 9.30am.
She added that in the week before the incident, her father had often been seen tidying the house, including sweeping and mowing the lawn, which was out of character for him.
“Over the past week, my late father kept cleaning the compound thoroughly, sweeping the grounds, mowing the lawn, and doing other chores as if he knew many people would come over,” she said.
Fire and Rescue Department personnel at the scene of a fatal crash involving a Hyundai Matrix car and a lorry at Kilometre 72.5 of Jalan Batu Pahat-Mersing in Kluang, Johor on October 2, 2026. — Picture from Facebook/This is Johor
It was reported yesterday that a married couple were killed while their two daughters were severely injured in a collision between a car and a lorry at Kilometre 72.5 of Jalan Batu Pahat-Mersing.
Kluang police chief ACP Bahrin Mohd Noh said the crash involved a lorry driven by a 34-year-old man heading from Kluang towards Kahang and a Hyundai Matrix travelling in the opposite direction.
He said investigations found that the Hyundai Matrix, driven by the 54-year-old local man, was believed to have lost control on the slippery road before veering into the opposite lane and colliding with the lorry. — Bernama

Title: Anwar hints at Budget 2027 help for hungry university students, urges youth to lead now
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today hinted that Budget 2027 could include measures to help university students struggling to afford food, saying the government was already looking into the issue.
Addressing thousands of youths at the Youth Economic Forum (YEF) 2026 here, Anwar said the government’s role included improving the quality of education and ensuring students could master Malay while strengthening their command of English and other languages.
“There are university students who say, we want to learn but we are hungry. We focus on it. Later I will announce during the Budget. Can’t announce it all,” he said, drawing loud cheers and applause from the audience.
Last Saturday, Anwar said he had heard of lower-income university students going hungry and surviving on instant noodles, adding that the Treasury already had several preliminary proposals to address the issue.
Anwar also stressed that young Malaysians should not see themselves merely as leaders of the future, but as leaders who could already work together to make a difference.
“The youth now, in the current narrative, certainly are leaders for the future. But the youth now should also help and lead the country together. You are not only leaders for the future, but also leaders now working together,” he said.
He urged young Malaysians of different ethnic backgrounds to reject racial and religious hatred, saying the country’s diversity should instead be harnessed as a strength.
“My word, I’m confident, if this is the new spirit, we will see our country advance fast and in 10 years’ time, it is not the Malaysia we know today, but we will see a new, vibrant, progressive, successful Malaysia,” he said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim speaks at the Youth Economic Forum 2026 at Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre on October 3, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
At the forum organised by the Perdana Fellows Alumni Association, Anwar also received six youth-led policy proposals based on a nationwide survey of more than 2,000 youths.
The proposals covered artificial intelligence, green entrepreneurship, skills development, public services, foreign direct investment and the establishment of a National Youth Economic Action Council as a platform for youths to contribute to economic policy.
He also received a memorandum on the proposals for Budget 2027.
YEF 2026 was held under the theme “Decoding the Next Decade: Advancing Malaysia’s Economic Frontier”.
Anwar received a warm welcome from the youths when he arrived for the forum, with many cheering and some chanting “PMX”, a reference to his position as Malaysia’s 10th prime minister.

Title: Sultan of Brunei arrives as Sepang hosts surprise F1 GP
Article:
SUBANG JAYA, Oct 3 — The Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, arrived in Malaysia today for a special visit in conjunction with the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), which began yesterday.
The special aircraft carrying His Majesty and the Brunei delegation, including Prince Abdul Mateen Bolkiah, landed safely at the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) base in Subang at 4.28pm.
They were welcomed by Tunku Temenggong Johor Tunku Idris Iskandar Al-Haj Sultan Ibrahim and Minister of Youth and Sports Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari.
His Majesty then inspected a guard of honour comprising two officers and 26 personnel of other ranks from the First Battalion of the Royal Malay Regiment, led by Captain Wan Amirul Syafiq Wan Zamri.
The Sepang International Circuit has been selected to host the 2026 F1 Gulf Air Bahrain GP, making the iconic circuit a temporary venue for the prestigious race.
Last July, Formula 1 confirmed that Malaysia would host the race, which is taking place until this Sunday.
This follows an agreement reached between Formula 1, the International Automobile Federation (FIA), and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
The agreement ensures the Bahrain GP remains on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race was cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
Malaysia previously hosted the Malaysian GP at Sepang from 1999 to 2017 before being dropped from the F1 calendar.
The return of the race to Malaysia is the result of diplomatic efforts involving His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and King Hamad Isa Al-Khalifa of Bahrain. — Bernama

Title: Manager held three more days over alleged RM200m tax reduction fraud
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — A financial and corporate services company manager has had his remand extended for another three days from tomorrow to assist in the investigation into the submission of documents containing false information to obtain a tax reduction worth approximately RM200 million.
The remand order against the man in his 40s was issued by Magistrate Illya Syaheedah Mohd Razif after the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) applied for the extension at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court today.
The suspect will be remanded until October 6, after his initial three-day remand period, which began last Thursday, ended today.
The media previously reported that preliminary investigations found the suspect was believed to have manipulated approximately 480 company accounts using fraudulent documents between 2018 and this year.
The man is also believed to have bribed an enforcement agency official to facilitate his activities, in addition to allegedly accumulating extraordinary wealth through the illicit operations.
Further investigations by the MACC led to raids at 12 locations, including the suspect’s office and residential premises.
During the operation, the MACC seized 25 luxury vehicles estimated to be worth approximately RM25 million.
The MACC also froze seven bank accounts, comprising four personal accounts and three company accounts, with a total value of approximately RM3 million.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, confirmed the remand extension and said the case is being investigated under Section 16 of the MACC Act 2009. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Pakatan to announce candidates in one or two weeks, says Amirudin
Article:
KLANG, Oct 3 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is expected to announce its candidates for the Melaka state election within the next one or two weeks, says PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
He said the coalition’s election machinery preparations have been progressing smoothly over the past two months.
“Our machinery is moving and ready. It is only the coordination, alignment, and mutual understanding that are yet to be finalised.
“God willing, in the near future — within a week or two — we will announce the candidates who will be contesting,” he said when met at the launch of the Tabung Warisan Anak Selangor (Tawas) ‘Tuaian Anak Harapan’ (Tuah) Initiative at the KSL Convention Centre here today.
On September 27, Melaka PH confirmed that seat distribution among its component parties at the state level for the Melaka state election had been completed.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari was reported as saying that the final seat arrangement, however, would be concluded following discussions among the PH Presidential Council, state PH leadership, and Amirudin as PH election director.
Meanwhile, asked about PH’s cooperation with Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) for the state election, Amirudin, who is also Selangor Menteri Besar, said PH remains open to discussions if there is room for such collaboration.
“If there is room, we will discuss. If not, we are ready to contest based on our existing capacity and understanding,” he said.
Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh previously announced that the state legislative assembly was dissolved effective September 23 after obtaining the consent of Melaka Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Mohd Rustam. — Bernama

Title: Time for a review: Creative industry seeks more Budget 2027 support as TV production rates lag behind costs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Creative industry players are calling on the government to maintain and enhance existing funds and incentives in the upcoming Budget 2027, while reviewing television programme production rates, which they say are no longer realistic amid rising costs.
Malaysian Film Producers Association deputy president Datuk Dr Yusof Haslam said government incentives and assistance should be maintained without cuts to safeguard the sustainability of the local creative industry ecosystem.
“I hope the government will look at this from a positive perspective and maintain all the assistance that has been provided to the industry. If there are plans for cuts, I hope they can be avoided,” he said when he appeared as a guest on Bernama TV’s ‘On E’ programme at Wisma Bernama here today.
Yusof also reminded industry players to uphold their responsibilities and integrity when managing any grant or allocation received from the government.
“Filmmakers must complete their films within the allocated budget and take the work seriously. These funds should not be used as a platform to make money for personal gain,” he said.
On the Film in Malaysia Incentive (FIMI), Yusof said the initiative has not only succeeded in attracting international production companies but has also provided crucial support for large-scale patriotic productions such as ‘MALBATT: Misi Bakara’.
He also appealed for television programme production rates, particularly those offered by Radio Televisyen Malaysia (RTM), to be reviewed in line with current cost increases, saying there had been no significant adjustment for almost four decades.
“I have been producing television dramas since 1985. At that time, the cost of a TV drama was within RM40,000. But after 40 years, the increase (in RTM’s payment) has only been about RM10,000.
“These rates should be reviewed every 10 years because if RTM increases its rates, other private companies will follow suit,” he said.
Meanwhile, film producer Nazira Ibrahim said the creative sector is a comprehensive ecosystem that requires consistent support, particularly in film marketing and distribution, to assist smaller-scale productions.
“Sometimes we have good products and compelling stories, but we have no avenue to market and distribute them to audiences. If the government can assist in developing these mechanisms, it could significantly raise the profile of our films and help them reach both local and international audiences,” she said.
On the RM10 million allocation for TVET Madani Creative Multimedia programmes, Nazira called for practical training on film sets to be prioritised over theoretical learning to produce highly skilled technical personnel behind the scenes.
“Skills are needed not only for those in front of the camera, such as the actors, scriptwriters and directors, but are equally important for people working behind the scenes, including camera operators, lighting crews and those handling visual effects, post-production and sound systems.
“Theoretical exposure alone is not enough. Students need industry training with production companies and should be exposed to actual film sets to see firsthand how a production operates,” she said.
Under Budget 2026, the government allocated RM110 million in incentives to encourage local and international film producers to create high-quality productions in Malaysia.
The initiative included a dedicated RM10 million allocation for the production of nation-building content as part of efforts to strengthen the orange economy ecosystem.
Budget 2027 is scheduled to be tabled in Parliament on October 9. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia cuts use of ozone-depleting HCFC by nearly 80pc, eyes full phase-out by 2030
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 3 — The National World Ozone Day 2026 celebration has reinforced Malaysia’s commitment to protecting the ozone layer and tackling climate change through a transition towards more sustainable and energy-efficient cooling technologies.
In a statement today, the Department of Environment (DOE) said the celebration, officiated by DOE Deputy Director-General (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon at a shopping centre here, carried the theme “Global Action for a Cooler Planet: Celebrating 10 Years of Sustainable Cooling under the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol”.
“This theme marks a decade of the Kigali Amendment, which focuses on reducing the consumption of high global warming potential hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), alongside accelerating the transition to sustainable and energy-efficient cooling technology.
“Malaysia, which ratified the Montreal Protocol in 1989, completely phased out chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and Halons in 2010.
“The nation has also reduced its hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs) consumption by nearly 80 per cent, aiming for a complete phase-out by 2030 under Stage III of the HCFC Phase-out Management Plan (HPMP III) and Stage I of the Kigali Implementation Plan,” the DOE said.
The DOE noted that these achievements stem from continuous collaboration between the government, industry, international development partners, relevant institutions, and the public to ensure Malaysia’s obligations under the Montreal Protocol and Kigali Amendment are effectively fulfilled.
Meanwhile, the DOE highlighted that Malaysia continues to strengthen environmental sustainability through a Refrigerant Lifecycle Management (RLM) approach to prevent harmful gas emissions and stimulate the circular economy.
“The DOE is also enhancing governance and industry competency by upgrading policies, legislation, and technical guidance for technicians. However, the implementation of the Montreal Protocol and Kigali Amendment demands a comprehensive commitment from industry, training institutes, the public, and key stakeholders,” the statement read.
Consequently, the DOE urged members of the public to play their part by selecting eco-friendly and energy-efficient cooling appliances, engaging DOE-certified technicians for maintenance services, ensuring the proper disposal of refrigerants, and consistently practising energy conservation.
The department affirmed it will continue ensuring policies, plans, and strategies related to the HCFC phase-out and HFC phase-down are effectively executed, alongside reinforcing legal frameworks, compliance, and enforcement regarding refrigerants in line with technological developments and Malaysia’s obligations under the Montreal Protocol.
“The 2026 World Ozone Day celebration does not merely commemorate past achievements; it serves as an ongoing reminder that efforts to safeguard the ozone layer and combat climate change must be sustained to secure a cleaner, healthier, and more sustainable environment for future generations,” the statement added.
World Ozone Day is celebrated annually on September 16 to commemorate the signing of the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer in 1987, as well as to raise public awareness on the importance of protecting the ozone layer and addressing climate change. — Bernama

Title: Police arrest motorcyclist for riding against traffic, crashing into two KL marathon participants
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — A 21-year-old motorcyclist was arrested after allegedly riding against traffic and crashing into two participants of the Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon (KLSCM) 2026 along Jalan Munshi Abdullah early today.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the incident occurred at about 6.15am after the motorcyclist, who was carrying a 19-year-old pillion rider, allegedly passed through a road closure marked by cones.
“The rider was ordered to stop by police personnel manning the road closure, but is believed to have fled by riding against the flow of traffic before crashing into two marathon participants who were running,” he said in a press statement.
One participant, a 50-year-old woman, suffered neck injuries and is receiving treatment at Prince Court.
The other victim, a 41-year-old man, sustained injuries to his right knee and hand.
Mohd Zamzuri said an initial alcohol screening on the motorcyclist returned a positive result, with an evidential breath alcohol reading of 164mg/100ml.
The motorcyclist and pillion rider were subsequently taken to Hospital Kuala Lumpur for blood and urine samples as part of further investigations.
The case is being investigated under Section 44(1A)(b) of the Road Transport Act 1987 and Section 186 of the Penal Code.
The motorcyclist has been remanded for three days from today until October 5, while the pillion rider has been remanded for two days until October 4, with both being held at the Dang Wangi police station lock-up.
Police urged witnesses or anyone with information on the incident to contact the Tun H.S. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or the nearest police station.

Title: Family of Bandar Utama school stabbing victim files civil suit against government agencies, boy and his parents
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — The mother and sister of the 16-year-old student who was fatally stabbed at a secondary school in Bandar Utama last year have filed a civil suit at the Kuala Lumpur High Court.
The family’s lawyer, Surendra Ananth, confirmed the suit that was filed on Thursday, adding that case management has been fixed for October 29.
“We have named a number of government agencies as defendants. We have named the parents of the boy who killed my daughter as defendants. We have also named the boy himself as a defendant,” the victim's mother, Wong Lee Ping, said in a statement today.
“With the increasing mental health challenges faced by our children today, we cannot choose to stay silent anymore.
“Grand statements and plans are insufficient. We cannot wait until more lives are lost before proper action is taken,” she added.
The intention to pursue civil action was first publicly announced on by Wong September.
Almost a year after her daughter, Yap Shing Xuen, was fatally stabbed on October 14 last year, Wong continues to seek answers over whether the tragedy could have been prevented.
At the time, the family said it planned to pursue a civil suit as the criminal case moved to the appeal stage following the Shah Alam High Court’s decision to acquit the teenage accused on the grounds of unsoundness of mind.
“Our lawyers will be filing a civil suit. Until the criminal proceedings are completed, we will not comment on the details. Our lawyers will explain those matters later,” Wong told a press conference on September 25.
The teenager accused of killing Yap, who was 14 at the time, was charged with murder at the Petaling Jaya Magistrates’ Court on October 22 last year.
The case subsequently underwent psychiatric assessment before being transferred to the Shah Alam High Court, where the trial was conducted in camera as the accused was a minor.
A psychiatric assessment found him fit to stand trial in January. He pleaded not guilty when the murder charge was read again at the High Court on February 12.
The trial began on August 3. On August 13, the High Court ordered the teenager to enter his defence after finding that the prosecution had established a
prima facie
case.
The defence closed its case on August 26 after two witnesses — the accused and a forensic psychiatrist — testified.
On September 14, High Court Judge Adlin Abdul Majid acquitted and discharged the teenager after finding that he was of unsound mind at the time of the offence, and ordered him to be placed at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta for a period to be approved by the Sultan of Selangor.
The Attorney General’s Chambers filed a notice of appeal at the Court of Appeal on September 22, challenging the acquittal.

Title: Malaysian pilot detained in Jakarta over alleged drug smuggling gets another 30 days in custody
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — The 39-year-old Malaysia Airlines pilot arrested in Jakarta in July over an alleged drug-smuggling operation remains in Indonesian custody after authorities extended his detention beyond the initial 60-day period.
Harian Metro
reported today that Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the extension was for another 30 days.
“The Malaysian police were informed by the Indonesian narcotics authorities. The case is still at the investigation and assessment stage,” he was quoted as saying.
He added that the detention could be extended for a further 30 days, based on information provided by Indonesian authorities.
Meanwhile, another pilot and six other individuals arrested in Malaysia over alleged links to the same drug syndicate have been detained for 60 days under the Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act 1985.
The investigation centres on allegations that the suspects were linked to drug-smuggling activities spanning Malaysia and Indonesia.
The Malaysia Airlines pilot was arrested at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in July after Indonesian authorities reportedly seized 15 packages containing about 70,000 capsules suspected to contain ecstasy and methamphetamine, weighing about 25kg in total.

Title: Sepang International Circuit working with partners, authorities to improve F1 traffic management
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 3 — The Sepang International Circuit (SIC) is working closely with its transport partners and relevant authorities to strengthen traffic, shuttle and crowd management arrangements for the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) 2026 race.
SIC said the measures followed challenges experienced by some fans travelling to and from the circuit yesterday, particularly during the evening departure period.
“The experience and safety of our fans remain our highest priority at Sepang International Circuit,” it said in a statement today.
The circuit operator advised fans attending the weekend race to plan their journeys in advance and refer to the latest travel information on its official social media channels.
A Formula 1 driver is seen during the free practice session for the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit October 2, 2026. — Bernama pic
Fans arriving at or departing from the circuit are also advised to follow the directions of officials and on-ground signage, as traffic arrangements may be adjusted according to prevailing conditions.
SIC thanked fans for their patience and cooperation, adding that it looked forward to welcoming them for an enjoyable and safe day at the circuit.
Yesterday, several ticket holders took to social media to voice their frustration over severe gridlock when exiting the circuit, with some reporting lengthy waits for shuttle buses connecting parking areas and public transport hubs.
In July, Formula 1 confirmed that Malaysia would host the Gulf Air Bahrain GP from October 2 to 4, following an agreement involving Formula 1, the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
The agreement keeps the Bahrain GP on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race was cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia. — Bernama
